'''Arlie Oswald Petters''', [[Order of the British Empire|MBE]] (born February 8, 1964) is a Belizean-American mathematical physicist, who is the Benjamin Powell Professor of mathematics and a professor of physics and economics at [[Duke University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fds.duke.edu/db/aas/math/faculty/petters|title=Arlie O. Petters, Benjamin Powell Professor & Professor of Mathematics, Physics, and Business Administration and Bass Fellow and Dean of Academic Affairs of Trinity College of Arts and Sciences and Professor of Economics|website=fds.duke.edu}}</ref> Petters became the provost at [[New York University Abu Dhabi]] effective September 1, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dhabi|first=NYU Abu|title=Arlie Petters Selected as Provost of NYU Abu Dhabi|url=https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/news/latest-news/community-life/2020/july/provost-petters-appointment-eng.html|access-date=2020-07-24|website=New York University Abu Dhabi|language=en}}</ref> Petters's research is focused on problems connected to the interplay of gravity and light and employing tools from [[astrophysics]], [[physical cosmology|cosmology]], [[general relativity]], [[high energy physics]], [[differential geometry]], [[singularity theory|singularities]], and [[probability theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/petters_arlie.html|title=Arlie O. Petters - Mathematicians of the African Diaspora|website=www.math.buffalo.edu}}</ref> His monograph "Singularity Theory and Gravitational Lensing" developed a mathematical theory of [[gravitational lensing]].  Petters was also the dean of academic affairs for Trinity College of Arts and Sciences and associate vice provost for undergraduate education at Duke University (2016-2019).<ref name="CV">{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.duke.edu/~petters/PETTERS-BIO-CV/Petters-CV.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae of Arlie O. Petters, Department of Mathematics, Duke University|access-date=2012-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120721230730/http://www.math.duke.edu/~petters/PETTERS-BIO-CV/Petters-CV.pdf|archive-date=2012-07-21|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Petters was raised by his grandparents in the rural community of [[Dangriga]], [[Belize]] (formerly Stann Creek Town, [[British Honduras]]).  His mother immigrated to Brooklyn, New York, and married a U.S. citizen, with Arlie joining them when he was 14 years old.<ref name="Times">[[Claudia Dreifus]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2003/05/27/science/a-conversation-with-arlie-petters-a-journey-to-bridge-math-and-the-cosmos.html A CONVERSATION WITH: ARLIE PETTERS: A Journey to Bridge Math and the Cosmos], ''[[The New York Times]]'', May 27, 2003.</ref>

Petters earned a [[Double degree#Dual degree programs|B.A./M.A.]] in [[Mathematics]] and [[Physics]] from [[Hunter College]], [[City University of New York|CUNY]] in 1986 with a thesis on [[Mathematics of general relativity|"The Mathematical Theory of General Relativity]]", and began his [[Ph.D.]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] Department of Mathematics in the same year. After two years of doctoral studies, he became an exchange scholar in the [[Princeton University]] Department of Physics ''in absentia'' from MIT. Petters earned his Ph.D. in mathematics in 1991 under advisors [[Bertram Kostant]] (MIT) and [[David Spergel]] (Princeton University).  He remained at MIT for two years as an instructor of [[pure mathematics]] (1991–1993) and then joined the faculty at Princeton University in the Department of Mathematics. He was an assistant professor at Princeton for five years (1993–1998) before moving to Duke University.<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|64811}}</ref>

Many media outlets have profiled Arlie Petters and his scholarship, including ''[[The New York Times]]'',<ref name="Times" /> [[Nova (American TV series)|NOVA]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/video/profile-arlie-petters/|title=Profile: Arlie Petters|website=www.pbs.org|date=24 July 2007 }}</ref> The HistoryMakers (a digital archive of oral histories featuring African-Americans and preserved at the [[Library of Congress]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=About {{!}} The HistoryMakers|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/about-us|access-date=2020-06-10|website=www.thehistorymakers.org|archive-date=2020-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621033916/https://www.thehistorymakers.org/about-us|url-status=dead}}</ref>),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehistorymakers.org/biography/arlie-petters-42|title=Arlie Petters's Biography|website=The HistoryMakers}}</ref>  Big Think,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bigthink.com/arliepetters|title=Big Think}}</ref> and Duke University's news outlet, ''The Chronicle''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2019/05/duke-university-arlie-petters-black-math-professor-u-s-diversify-field|title=Arlie Petters is one of the few tenured black mathematicians. He wants to diversify his field|website=The Chronicle |date=20 May 2019 }}</ref>

== Research ==
Petters is known for his work in the mathematical theory of [[gravitational lensing]].

Over the ten-year period from 1991 to 2001, Petters systematically developed a mathematical theory of weak-deflection gravitational lensing, beginning with his 1991 MIT Ph.D. thesis on "Singularities in Gravitational Microlensing".<ref>
A. O. Petters, Ph.D. Thesis, MIT, Department of Mathematics (1991):
"Singularities in Gravitational Microlensing."
[http://library.mit.edu/F/8Y3V5E76URA8YQVNYMEE461M4XHC29JX9II7AI8LCN4IEBQYMA-85003?func=find-acc&acc_sequence=009012734]
</ref> In a series of papers, he and his collaborators resolved an array of theoretical problems in weak-deflection gravitational lensing covering image counting, fixed-point images, image magnification, image time delays, local geometry of caustics, global geometry of caustics, wavefronts, caustic surfaces, and caustic surfing.<ref>
Section A, "Research Period 1991–2001," Curriculum Vitae of Arlie O. Petters, Department of
Mathematics, Duke University
[http://www.math.duke.edu/~petters]
</ref> His work culminated in book, entitled ''Singularity Theory and Gravitational Lensing'' (Springer 2012)'','' which he co-authored with Harold Levine and Joachim Wambganns.  This book, which addressed the question, "What is the universe made of?", systematically created a framework of stability and genericity for k-plane gravitational lensing.<ref name=":0" /> The book drew upon powerful tools from the theory of singularities and put the subject of weak-deflection k-plane gravitational lensing on a rigorous and unified mathematical foundation.<ref name=":0">
''Singularity Theory and Gravitational Lensing'',
A. O. Petters, H. Levine, and J. Wambsganss (Birkhauser, Boston, 2001).
Amazon.com
[https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000U8UVVA]
</ref>

Following his 1991–2001 body of mathematical lensing work, Petters turned to more astrophysical lensing issues from 2002 to 2005. In collaboration with astronomers, he applied some of the mathematical theory in [AP13] to help develop a practical diagnostic test for the presence of dark substructures in galaxies lensing quasars;<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Keeton | first1=Charles R. | last2=Gaudi | first2=B. Scott | last3=Petters | first3=A. O. | title=Identifying Lenses with Small-Scale Structure. I. Cusp Lenses | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | date=2003 | volume=598 | issue=1 | pages=138–161 | doi=10.1086/378934 | arxiv=astro-ph/0210318 | bibcode=2003ApJ...598..138K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Keeton | first1=Charles R. | last2=Gaudi | first2=B. Scott | last3=Petters | first3=A. O. | title=Identifying Lenses with Small-Scale Structure. II. Fold Lenses | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | date=2005 | volume=635 | issue=1 | pages=35–59 | doi=10.1086/497324 | arxiv=astro-ph/0503452 | bibcode=2005ApJ...635...35K }}</ref> classify the local [[astrometric]] (centroid) and [[photometry (astronomy)|photometric]] curves of an extended source when it crosses fold and cusp caustics due to generic lenses;<ref name="www.arxiv.org">{{cite journal | last1=Gaudi | first1=B. Scott | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Gravitational Microlensing near Caustics. I. Folds | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | date=2002 | volume=574 | issue=2 | pages=970–984 | doi=10.1086/341063 | arxiv=astro-ph/0112531 | bibcode=2002ApJ...574..970G }}</ref><ref name="O. Petters, Astrophys 2002">{{cite journal | last1=Gaudi | first1=B. Scott | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Gravitational Microlensing near Caustics. II. Cusps | journal=The Astrophysical Journal | date=2002 | volume=580 | issue=1 | pages=468–489 | doi=10.1086/343114 | arxiv=astro-ph/0206162 | bibcode=2002ApJ...580..468G }}</ref> predict the quantitative astrometric curve's shape produced by Galactic binary lenses.<ref name="www.arxiv.org" /><ref name="O. Petters, Astrophys 2002" />  The classified local properties of the astrometric curves revealed a characteristic S-shape for fold crossings, parabolic and swallowtail features for cusp crossings, and a jump discontinuity for crossings over the fold arcs merging into a cusp. Petters, Levine, and Wambgamnns also developed a formula to calculate the size of the jump.

During the period from 2005 to 2007, Petters collaborated with astronomers and physicists to explore gravitational lensing in directions beyond its traditional confines in astronomy. In a series of three mathematical physics papers published written with the astronomer Charles R. Keeton, he utilized higher-order gravitational lensing effects by compact bodies to test different theories of gravity with the general theory of relativity of Einstein among them. These papers computed beyond the standard weak-deflection limit the first- and second-order corrections to the image positions, magnifications, and time delays due to lensing in general relativity and alternative gravitational theories describable within the [[PPN formalism]],<ref name="O. Petters, Phys 2005">{{cite journal | last1=Keeton | first1=Charles R. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Formalism for testing theories of gravity using lensing by compact objects: Static, spherically symmetric case | journal=Physical Review D | date=2005 | volume=72 | issue=10 | article-number=104006 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.72.104006 | arxiv=gr-qc/0511019 | bibcode=2005PhRvD..72j4006K }}</ref> and even determined lensing invariants for the PPN family of models.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Keeton | first1=Charles R. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Formalism for testing theories of gravity using lensing by compact objects. II. Probing post-post-Newtonian metrics | journal=Physical Review D | date=2006 | volume=73 | issue=4 | article-number=044024 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.73.044024 | arxiv=gr-qc/0601053 | bibcode=2006PhRvD..73d4024K }}</ref> Their findings were applied to the Galactic [[black hole]], [[binary pulsar]]s, and [[gravitational microlensing]] scenarios to make testable predictions about lensed images and their time delays.<ref name="O. Petters, Phys 2005" /> Another paper took on the difficult issue of how to test [[Higher dimension|hyperspace]] models like [[braneworld]] gravity that postulate an extra dimension to physical space. The paper developed a semi-classical wave theory of braneworld black hole lensing and used that theory along with braneworld cosmology to predict a testable signature of microscopic braneworld black holes on gamma-ray light.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Keeton | first1=Charles R. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Formalism for testing theories of gravity using lensing by compact objects. III. Braneworld gravity | journal=Physical Review D | date=2006 | volume=73 | issue=10 | article-number=104032 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.73.104032 | arxiv=gr-qc/0603061 | bibcode=2006PhRvD..73j4032K }}</ref><ref>
[http://www.dukenews.duke.edu/2006/05/braneworld.html "Scientist Predict How to Detect a Fourth Dimension," Duke News] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090929232532/http://www.dukenews.duke.edu/2006/05/braneworld.html |date=September 29, 2009 }}</ref> Additionally, in a 2007 paper, Petters and M.C. Werner found a system of equations that can be applied to test the [[Cosmic Censorship Hypothesis]] observationally using the realistic case of lensing by a [[Kerr black hole]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Werner | first1=M. C. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=Magnification relations for Kerr lensing and testing cosmic censorship | journal=Physical Review D | date=2007 | volume=76 | issue=6 | article-number=064024 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.76.064024 | arxiv=0706.0132 | bibcode=2007PhRvD..76f4024W }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.duke.edu/2007/09/nakedsingular.html|title="Seeking Objects Weirder than Black Holes," Duke News|access-date=2009-08-12|archive-date=2010-01-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100108030821/http://news.duke.edu/2007/09/nakedsingular.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Petters's previous work (1991–2007) dealt with non-random gravitational lensing. Starting in 2008, his research program focused on developing a mathematical theory of random (stochastic) gravitational lensing. In two papers, Petters, Rider, and Teguia took first steps in creating a mathematical theory of stochastic gravitational microlensing. They characterized to several asymptotic orders the probability densities of random time delay functions, lensing maps, and shear maps in stochastic microlensing and determined a Kac-Rice type formula for the global expected number of images due to a general stochastic lens system.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Petters | first1=A. O. | last2=Rider | first2=B. | last3=Teguia | first3=A. M. | title=A mathematical theory of stochastic microlensing. I. Random time delay functions and lensing maps | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | date=2009 | volume=50 | issue=7 | article-number=072503 | doi=10.1063/1.3158854 | arxiv=0807.0232 | bibcode=2009JMP....50g2503P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Petters | first1=A. O. | last2=Rider | first2=B. | last3=Teguia | first3=A. M. | title=A mathematical theory of stochastic microlensing. II. Random images, shear, and the Kac–Rice formula | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | date=2009 | volume=50 | issue=12 | article-number=122501 | doi=10.1063/1.3267859 | arxiv=0807.4984 | bibcode=2009JMP....50l2501P }}</ref> The work forms a concrete framework from which extensions to more general random maps can be made. In two additional papers, he and Aazami found geometric universal magnification [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]]s of higher-order caustics occurring in lensing and caustics produced by generic general maps up to codimension five.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Aazami | first1=A. B. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=A universal magnification theorem for higher-order caustic singularities | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | date=2009 | volume=50 | issue=3 | article-number=032501 | doi=10.1063/1.3081055 | arxiv=0811.3447 | bibcode=2009JMP....50c2501A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Aazami | first1=A. B. | last2=Petters | first2=A. O. | title=A universal magnification theorem. II. Generic caustics up to codimension five | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | date=2009 | volume=50 | issue=8 | article-number=082501 | doi=10.1063/1.3179163 | arxiv=0904.2236 | bibcode=2009JMP....50h2501A }}</ref><ref>[http://news.science360.gov/archives/20090416.aspx National Science Foundation, Science360 News Server, April 16, 2009]</ref> The invariants hold with a probability of 1 for random lenses and thereby form important consistency checks for research on random image magnifications of sources near stable caustics.

==Social outreach==
Petters has served as director of the Reginaldo Howard Memorial Scholarship program at [[Duke University]].<ref>
[http://web.duke.edu/reginaldohoward/index.php The Reginaldo Howard Memorial Scholarship program, Duke University]
</ref> He has also been active in the African-American community particularly through his mentoring, recruiting, and lecturing.<ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2002/12/math-professor-reaches-out-minorities |title=Math Professor Reaches Out to Minorities |last=Prabhu |first=Malavika |date=December 4, 2002 |newspaper=Duke Chronicle |archive-url=https://archive.today/20080907093330/http://media.www.dukechronicle.com/media/storage/paper884/news/2002/12/04/News/Math-Professor.Reaches.Out.To.Minorities-1461689.shtml |archive-date=2008-09-07 |url-status=unfit |accessdate=2018-12-08}}
</ref><ref>Arlie O. Petters, Curriculum Vitae--''Service to Underrepresented Minority Community,'' Department of Mathematics, Duke University [http://www.math.duke.edu/~petters/]</ref> He has received several community service awards for his social outreach.<ref name="Duke Magazine, Star Professor">[http://www.dukemagazine.duke.edu/dukemag/issues/010203/depupd.html Duke Magazine, "Star Professor"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829102501/http://www.dukemagazine.duke.edu/dukemag/issues/010203/depupd.html |date=August 29, 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://services.math.duke.edu/~petters/|title=Arlie O. Petters|website=services.math.duke.edu}}</ref> Petters is the first tenured African-American professor in mathematics at Duke University.<ref name="Duke Magazine, Star Professor" /> He is very involved in the Belizean community and founded the Petters Research Institute<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pribelize.org/|title=Home - Petters Research Institute|website=www.pribelize.org|access-date=2009-03-29|archive-date=2009-06-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090623201754/http://www.pribelize.org/|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2005 to help train Belizean young people in STEM fields and foster STEM entrepreneurship.<ref>[http://www.7newsbelize.com/sstory.php?nid=11902 7 News Belize]</ref><ref>Computer assembly course for Belizean students by Petters Research Institute and the Belize Defence Force [http://www.pribelize.org/Academy2007/index.html] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107085324/http://www.pribelize.org/Academy2007/index.html |date=2009-01-07 }}</ref> He has written five books, three of them science and mathematics problem-solving books for Belizean students.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://amandala.com.bz/news/|title=Amandala Newspaper &#124; "Belize's Leading Newspaper"|website=amandala.com.bz}}</ref><ref>Publications of Arlie O. Petters, Department of Mathematics, Duke University [http://fds.duke.edu/db/aas/math/faculty/petters/publications]</ref>  Some of his entrepreneurial work was conducted while he was a professor of business administration at Duke's [[Fuqua School of Business]] (2008–2017).<ref name="CV"/>  Petters also served the Government of Belize as chairman of the Council of Science Advisers to the prime minister of Belize (2010–2013).<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120722013432/http://www.belize.gov.bz/ct.asp?xItem=2110&ctNode=633&mp=27|title=Government of Belize Official Press Release, April 28, 2010}},</ref><ref name="CV" />

== Awards and honors ==
Petters has received numerous awards and honors.<ref>Arlie Petters, official Curriculum Vitae, Department of Mathematics, Duke University [http://fds.duke.edu/db/aas/math/faculty/petters]</ref>  He was won an [[Alfred P. Sloan]] Research Fellowship in Mathematics (1998),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sloan.org/fellowships/list|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519162228/http://www.sloan.org/fellowships/list|url-status=dead|title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, list of past fellows|archivedate=May 19, 2011}}</ref> and a CAREER award from the [[National Science Foundation]] (1998),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/crssprgm/career/awards/fy98/state.htm#nj |title=National Science Foundation, FY 98 CAREER Awardes (New Jersey) |access-date=2018-04-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303165043/http://www.nsf.gov/crssprgm/career/awards/fy98/state.htm#nj |archive-date=2016-03-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was the first winner of the [[Blackwell-Tapia Prize]] (2002).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=495|title=SIAM News}}</ref> He was selected in 2006 by the [[National Academy of Sciences]] to be part of a permanent Portrait Collection of Outstanding African-Americans in Science, Engineering, and Medicine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AAHP_Database_Bio_Petters|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100629121852/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AAHP_Database_Bio_Petters|url-status=dead|title=National Academy of Sciences, African-American History Program|archivedate=June 29, 2010}}</ref> In 2008 Petters was also included among the Human Relations Associates' list of "The Twenty-Five Greatest Scientists of African Ancestry,"going back to the eighteenth century.<ref>Human Relations Associates, The Twenty-Five Greatest Scientists of African Ancestry {{cite web
 |url=http://hrassoc.net/blog/modules/news/article.php?storyid%3D17
 |accessdate=2009-09-22
 |title=Archived copy
 |archive-date=2012-02-22
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120222234141/http://hrassoc.net/blog/modules/news/article.php?storyid=17
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref> He received an honorary Doctor of Science from his alma mater, [[Hunter College]], in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hunter.cuny.edu/communications/news/hunter-headlines|title=Hunter Headlines — Hunter College|website=www.hunter.cuny.edu|date=15 July 2024 }}</ref> Petters was named by the Queen of the United Kingdom in 2008 to membership in the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire.<ref>[http://www.london-gazette.co.uk/issues/58564/supplements/42 London Gazette], [http://www.dukenews.duke.edu/2008/01/petters_award.html Duke Today] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080919212109/http://www.dukenews.duke.edu/2008/01/petters_award.html |date=September 19, 2008 }}</ref> In recognition of his scientific accomplishments and service to society, Petters's birthplace—[[Dangriga]], Belize—honored him in 2009 by naming a road ''Dr. Arlie Petters Street''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dukeresearch.blogspot.com/2010/01/putting-his-name-on-map.html|title=Duke Research Blog: Putting His Name on the Map|first=Karl Leif|last=Bates|date=January 13, 2010}}</ref> He became in 2011 the first Belizean to receive the Caribbean American Heritage Award for Excellence in Science and Technology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edition.channel5belize.com/archives/63320|title=Arlie Petters wins award &#124; Channel5Belize.com|first=ky Says|last=Louisville}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-05-05.</ref> and the first Belizean American to be Grand Marshal of the Central American Day Parade in [[Los Angeles]], where he received honors from the mayor and from the [[Confederación Centroamericana y del Caribe de Fútbol|Confederation Centroamericana]] (COFECA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cofeca.org/|title=Confederacion Centroamericana|website=Confederacion Centroamericana}}</ref><ref name="CV" /> Petters was recognized by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2017 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Arlie Petters|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/arlie-petters/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180207192801/http://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com:80/honorees/arlie-petters/ |archive-date=2018-02-07 |access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>
